items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: When we finished we met the manager of this music publishers and all

ctx.x: get an apartment at $35 a week? We you get that at? You ought to be ashamed of yourself thinking like that. There ain't nothing been handed out since I've been born.

So we go to the house, open up the trunk, take out our roller skates -- but I didn't tell you, this fella when we got to New York -- forgot to tell you that the man took us the next day down to Leo Feist, the biggest music publisher in New York City. He took us to Leo Feist on 7th Avenue between 47th and 46th -- 48th I think, on 7th Avenue. He took us there to let them hear who it is it was that they brought back to New York. They had a lot of entertainers there, singing songs, learning songs and so forth, that's…

unless he tells us, unless he takes us. Okay.
This is the beginning. Kids are not allowed around New York. Understand? September 1919. Would you believe that I walked out of this man's office, about three months later after he said that, I done play Staten Island, come to his office to get the money, he raised his hand, walked out of the office and for the first time about three months later I walked back -- get your roller skates -- put our skates on, I said, Buck, put your skates on good, man because you're…
